name: Socialist-oriented market economy
summary: The official economic doctrine of the Communist Party of Vietnam since the Doi Moi reforms of 1986: a multi-sector market economy with state, collective and private ownership, in which the state sector plays the leading role and the Party directs the transition towards socialism. Markets are treated as a transitional tool for developing productive forces, not as socialism itself, and are paired with one-party leadership, Marxism-Leninism and Ho Chi Minh Thought, and an emphasis on national independence.
scope: The Vietnamese doctrine as set out in Article 51 of the 2013 Constitution, the Party's 2011 platform and General Secretary Nguyen Phu Trong's 2021 article on socialism and the path to it. It excludes China's 'socialist market economy' (covered separately as socialism with Chinese characteristics) and academic market socialism, in which markets are central to socialism itself. Positions on topics the Party texts never address are inferred from Vietnamese law and practice and marked low confidence.

sources.title: Constitution of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam (1992, rev. 2013)

sources.usedFor: Article 51 (the economy), Article 4 (Party leadership), property, land, rights, religion, defence, armed forces and social provisions.

sources.title: Đổi Mới

sources.usedFor: Reform history: decollectivisation, private sector and foreign investment laws, SOE reform, limits on political reform, inequality.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Art. 58 commits the State to health insurance for the entire people with priority for highlanders and minorities, though Doi Moi moved care to a hybrid market system with out-of-pocket costs (s4).

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Art. 57 has the State protect workers and build harmonious labour relations; an adherent backs rising wage floors as growth allows, but the sources never discuss minimum wage levels directly.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Party treats the market as a tool for allocating resources within a state-led, socialist-oriented framework, and says the market economy it builds is not a capitalist one, so it rejects unqualified market superiority.

public-ownership.rationale: Art. 51 gives the state economic sector the 'leading role' and Art. 53 makes land and natural resources property of the entire people, but private firms are equal constituents so ownership is mixed rather than total.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Trong ties growth to 'social progress and equality in every stage', implying progressive taxation, but none of the sources set out tax rates on the rich.

unions-good.rationale: Art. 9 names the Vietnam Trade Union as a Fatherland Front member and Art. 57 aims at harmonious labour relations; unions exist, but as Party-led bodies rather than independent bargaining agents.

property-fundamental.rationale: Art. 32 protects private ownership and inheritance, yet allows requisition for defence and national interest, and Art. 53/54 keep land under state ownership, so property is protected but not a near-absolute right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Art. 52 has the State coordinate the economy and Art. 51 gives the state sector the lead, so tight regulation of firms fits the state-managed market model.

cut-welfare.rationale: Art. 59 commits the State to social security and aid for the elderly, disabled and poor, so cutting welfare as harmful dependency contradicts the stated programme.

worker-ownership.rationale: The programme names the working class as ruling base but ownership is via state, collective and private forms (Art. 51); workers collectively owning their own firms is not the model, and cooperatives are only one sector.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Art. 14 allows rights to be restricted for national security and social order, which implies acceptance of security surveillance, though no source discusses surveillance directly.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Art. 14 lets rights be restricted for social morality and health of the community, and Vietnamese policy is strongly prohibitionist; inferred, sources do not discuss drugs.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Art. 5 strictly forbids acts of national discrimination and division, and Art. 25 lets the law regulate speech, so legal restriction of hate speech fits; inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: Official doctrine stresses collective leadership by the Party and democratic centralism (Art. 8) rather than a leader bypassing institutions; inferred from the structure of Party rule.

state-harmful.rationale: Trong's article presents the socialist rule-of-law state as the instrument of the people's mastery and a core pillar, so the claim that the state is unnecessary and harmful is directly opposed.

limit-guns.rationale: Vietnam bans civilian firearm ownership and armed force belongs to the state and Party (Art. 65); inferred since the sources do not address civilian guns as such.

empower-police-military.rationale: Art. 64-65 build national defence and security around the people's armed forces as a core, loyal to the Party and State, so strengthening them is consistent.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Art. 14 allows restrictions for social morality, and sex work is illegal in Vietnam; inferred, the sources do not address it.

decide-locally.rationale: Art. 8 sets democratic centralism and Art. 52 stresses 'unity of the national economy' alongside decentralization, so national direction prevails over maximal localism.

rehabilitation.rationale: Sources do not address penal philosophy; Vietnam combines rehabilitative language with a retained death penalty and strict punishment.

traditional-family.rationale: Art. 60 aims at a Vietnamese family that is 'well off, progressive, and happy' and Art. 58 places family duties on the citizen, so the family is treated as a foundation of society.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Vietnam does not recognise same-sex marriage and the Party has not championed it; inferred, the sources do not address it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Art. 58 mentions family planning as state policy and abortion is legal in Vietnam; inferred, not discussed in the sources.

more-religion-public.rationale: Art. 24 guarantees freedom of belief but forbids exploiting religion to violate the law, and Party doctrine is Marxist-Leninist, so a larger public role for religion is not sought.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Art. 5 stresses equality of nationalities and priority development for minorities, but historical racial injustice in the Western sense is not an issue the sources take up.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Art. 26 guarantees gender equality and bans sex discrimination, but the sources take no position on whether gender is a social construct.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Art. 60 calls for a Vietnamese culture 'deeply imbued with the national identity', and Trong calls national independence the fundamental guideline.

gradual-change.rationale: Trong describes the path to socialism as long and gradual through a transitional period, and Doi Moi was a step-by-step reform led by the Party (s4).

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration is not a live issue in Vietnam's programme; Art. 48 treats foreign residents with protection, so no position is documented.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Trong stresses independence and self-reliance with international integration, so Vietnam joins institutions but does not seek to hand them more power over states; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Doi Moi opened to foreign investment and trade and the Party seeks to be 'well integrated with the world', though the state manages integration and strategic sectors.

nation-first.rationale: Policy pairs independence and self-reliance with 'peace, cooperation and development', so adherents neither put the nation strictly first nor subordinate it to global cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Foreign policy is founded on independence and non-interference, so military intervention abroad for rights is opposed; inferred from this principle.

open-borders.rationale: Art. 44 and 45 stress duty to defend the Fatherland and territorial integrity, and nothing suggests open borders; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Trong says growth must accompany social progress and Art. 50 pursues industrialisation and modernisation, so limiting growth is rejected even while environmental protection is stressed.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Art. 63 commits the State to respond to climate change and Trong calls environmental protection 'an existential issue', but drastic costly action sits behind development priority.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The platform and Art. 62 make science and technology a primary national policy and call for a knowledge-based economy, an optimistic view of technological progress.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Vietnam has planned nuclear power for energy security and Art. 63 encourages new energy; inferred, not directly discussed.

revolution-justified.rationale: The Party's legitimacy rests on the revolution and the socialist goal, though its current line stresses gradual transition rather than new revolutions.

experts-over-public.rationale: Art. 6 stresses the people's direct and indirect democracy, but Party and technocratic direction is strong; adherents are split in emphasis.

central-planning.rationale: The Party rejects Soviet-style central planning as skipping the market stage, though it still uses five-year plans, so it denies that full planning beats markets.

socialized-markets.rationale: The model keeps markets with state, collective and private owners; the Party accepts markets under public leadership, though workers' ownership is not the mechanism.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land is owned by the entire people under Art. 53 with use rights, so a land tax replacing others is neither stated nor ruled out.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Art. 32 explicitly protects the right of inheritance, so heavy inheritance taxes sit against the constitutional text; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Art. 59 builds a targeted social security system for the poor and elderly, not an unconditional income for all adults; no source supports universal payments.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Doi Moi opened trade while the Party shields strategic state industries; sources do not give a clear tariff doctrine.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Art. 51 gives the state sector the leading role and Art. 52 has the State coordinate the economy, so directing investment toward strategic industries is central.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Art. 51 gives the state sector the lead and Art. 53 vests land in the whole people, so broad small ownership is accepted but is not the programme's organising principle.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Trong presents communism as the long-term goal, which classically means the end of wage labour, but the transitional model keeps money and wages for the foreseeable future.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Art. 55 has the State guarantee the value of the national currency under unified management, so abolishing the central bank is opposed.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Labour relations are mediated by Party-linked trade unions (Art. 9, 57), but state bodies setting wages and prices together is not the model; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: Art. 4 declares the Communist Party of Vietnam the 'leading force of the State and society', stating this explicitly and as foundational.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The state is a socialist republic founded in revolution, and Art. 2 vests power in the people, so a hereditary monarch is rejected; inferred.

democracy-best.rationale: Trong calls democracy 'the nature of the socialist regime' but criticises Western multiparty systems, so adherents embrace 'socialist democracy' while rejecting the liberal reading of this statement.

direct-votes.rationale: Art. 6 allows direct democracy and the Assembly can hold referendums, but the model is representative with democratic centralism; frequent popular votes on laws are not used.

workers-councils.rationale: Power rests in the National Assembly and People's Councils under Party leadership (Art. 4, 6), not in workers' councils replacing parliament.

right-to-secede.rationale: Art. 5 defines Vietnam as 'the unified nation of all nationalities' and acts of national division are strictly forbidden.

natural-rulers.rationale: Official doctrine says the people are masters, though the vanguard party claims a leading role; adherents reject natural rulers, inferred.

political-violence-never.rationale: The state's legitimacy rests on a revolutionary struggle and armed force, so it does not hold violence is never justified, though it stresses peace today.

war-builds-character.rationale: Foreign policy emphasises peace and cooperation, and the Party does not celebrate war as improving the nation.

separate-church-state.rationale: Art. 24 protects belief but religion has no role in state power, and the Party is explicitly Marxist-Leninist.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Art. 8 requires the state to rule by the Constitution and laws under Marxist-Leninist doctrine, so scripture is not a source of law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Art. 64-65 make defence the business of the entire people with the armed forces loyal to Party and State, so private provision is rejected.

military-superiority.rationale: The programme stresses strong all-people defence (Art. 64) but aims at defence of territory and peace, not military superiority over rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Art. 5 defines Vietnam as a unified nation of all nationalities that are equal, rejecting single-ethnicity nationhood.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Marxism-Leninism is the foundation, but Trong says socialism seeks 'social consensus rather than social opposition', so class conflict is no longer stressed as the main driver.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Trong demands 'social progress and equality in every stage', yet the model tolerates market inequality and rewards by contribution in the transition (s4 Gini).

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Art. 53 vests land in the entire people managed by the State, so authority over traditional lands rests with the state; Art. 5 only promises minorities support.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The sources contain no stated demand for reparations; the state emphasises independence and cooperation with former adversaries.

civilizational-union.rationale: Policy centres on national independence and sovereignty and 'unity in diversity' within the nation, so civilisational political unions are not sought; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Art. 15 says citizens' rights are inseparable from duties and Art. 56 urges saving and anti-luxury, which opposes treating self-interest as a moral good.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Art. 15 says citizens' rights are inseparable from duties and Art. 14 and 15 limit rights by national interests, putting duty to the community prominently.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Art. 63 protects nature and biodiversity but in terms of managed resources and development; no source takes up intrinsic value.

limit-population.rationale: Art. 58 mentions family planning as policy, which Vietnam has used, but later policy relaxed it; inferred and mixed.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Art. 50 commits to industrialisation and modernisation, so calling industrial civilisation a disaster is opposed.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Trong calls for knowledge-based economy and rapid modernisation, but the Party also prizes stability of institutions; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Sources do not address the topic.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Sources do not address AI governance; digital government is promoted but Party control is retained.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Art. 14 allows rights restrictions for national security and the state controls information (Art. 60), so unbreakable encryption would not be endorsed; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: The programme is oriented to building socialism in the future, not restoring a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Doi Moi was framed as pragmatic reform but the Party insists that policy remains within Marxism-Leninism and socialist orientation, so adherents are split.

direct-action.rationale: Political change is channelled through the Party-led state, Assembly and Fatherland Front (Art. 6, 9), not direct action outside them.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources do not address this ethic of revolutionary means.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Art. 50 aims at industrialisation and modernisation, so a return to foraging is plainly rejected.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The programme builds an advanced economy on developed productive forces; abolition belongs only to a remote communist stage.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Trong names communism as the ultimate goal where distribution is by need, but the transition distributes mainly by work, so this is a long-run aim only.

production-for-use.rationale: The model is explicitly a market economy producing for profit in private firms, though the state sector has social goals; the Party treats the profit motive as a transitional tool.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Art. 51 treats private enterprise as an important and protected constituent of the economy, and the Party admits capitalists into membership, so profit is not branded exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Marxism-Leninism is the foundation and the Party claims to be the working class vanguard, but current texts speak of the people's mastery and a rule-of-law state rather than proletarian dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Doi Moi's Resolution 10 ended obligatory cooperatives and restored household land-use rights, so collective farming has been abandoned as the rule.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Doctrine is Marxist-Leninist but present policy stresses peace and integration with capitalist economies, so imperialism-war determinism is not stated.

taxation-theft.rationale: Art. 47 makes paying taxes a citizen's duty, so taxation as theft is firmly rejected.

harm-principle.rationale: Art. 14 lets rights be restricted for national defence, security, social morality and health, which exceeds a harm-only limit.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Art. 15 ties rights to duties and national interests and Art. 5 gives rights to nationalities, so rights are not solely individual.

conscription.rationale: Art. 45 says the citizen 'must fulfil his military obligation', directly supporting conscription.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The model gives primacy to participation through the Party-led system and national loyalty (Art. 44), so exit as the chief check is rejected.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is framed as serving the people under Party leadership, not a firm with customers; the sources do not use a business model.

positive-liberty.rationale: Art. 3 aims at all-round development and Art. 59 promises welfare, housing and health, treating material means as conditions for freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Media are directed under Party leadership (Art. 60), so the claim that they outweigh elected officials runs against official theory; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Art. 5 and 16 prohibit racial and national discrimination and the Party embraces equality of nationalities; inferred, not discussed directly.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation is through the Assembly and Fatherland Front with Party leadership (Art. 6, 9), not families and trade bodies replacing parties.

total-state.rationale: Art. 32-33 protect private property and enterprise, so the state does not direct every area of economic life though the Party leads culture and politics.

national-rebirth.rationale: Trong speaks of a strong nation and affluent people but not of a decadence needing radical rebirth; no stated position.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Foreign policy is stated as independence, peace and non-interference, so territorial expansion is rejected.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Art. 2 and 8 rest authority on the Constitution and law and the people, not oaths between lords and followers.

bound-labor.rationale: Doi Moi restored household farmers' land-use rights and free sale, the opposite of binding farmers to land.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Marxism-Leninism treats ideas as class-shaped, but official texts present their own science as objective, so adherents split.

universal-morality.rationale: Trong calls for 'progressive and humanistic values' in a diverse culture, but also claims a scientific socialist worldview; no clear stance on universal moral truths.

single-common-good.rationale: The Party claims to represent 'the interests of the working class, the toiling people and the whole nation' (Art. 4), a single national interest rather than balancing groups.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The sources do not address this; Vietnam maintains relations with Israel while supporting Palestinian rights.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Art. 9 includes overseas Vietnamese in the Fatherland Front, but no statement of a legal right of return is documented.

revive-national-language.rationale: Vietnamese is already the national language (Art. 5); the case of revival does not arise.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Trong stresses 'the people as owners' and grassroots democracy, but company governance by employee and public vote is not the model.

school-vouchers.rationale: Art. 61 has the State prioritise investment in education and free compulsory secondary schooling; vouchers to any school are not the model.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Art. 55 asks for effective and transparent budget management, but the Party also uses state investment to drive growth; no clear stance.

economic-freedom.rationale: The Party insists political leadership stays with the Communist Party while promoting economic reform, so it denies that political freedom depends on economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Art. 8 emphasises rule by Constitution and laws and an anticorruption drive, though cadres' moral example is also stressed; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Trong calls national independence linked with socialism the 'fundamental guideline' of the revolution, endorsing each nation's right to self-rule.

force-without-un.rationale: Foreign policy is built on independence, peace and respect for international law, so unilateral force abroad is opposed.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Art. 24 protects belief while the Party stands on scientific socialism; adherents do not make reason the sole guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Social security provisions apply to citizens (Art. 34, 59), but the sources do not take up immigrants' eligibility.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Art. 35 makes work a right and Art. 59 provides aid to the poor and disabled; there is no stated work requirement.

class-collaboration.rationale: Trong says socialism 'requires and is also able to cultivate social consensus rather than social opposition', and Art. 57 aims at harmonious labour relations.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Art. 60 calls for a culture imbued with national identity and Art. 41 protects access to cultural values, so sacrificing inherited cultural institutions to novelty is rejected.

dominated-front.rationale: Foreign policy is 'independence, self-reliance, peace, cooperation' and balanced relations with all powers, so a bloc against the West is not sought.

workers-nation.rationale: The programme is both a working-class party and a national one; Art. 2 bases state power on the alliance of workers, peasants and intelligentsia within the nation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Art. 26 guarantees equal rights for women and men in all fields and prohibits sex discrimination.

ban-interest.rationale: Art. 55 sets the national currency and the programme builds a market economy with banking; banning interest is inconsistent.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Art. 5 and 16 forbid national discrimination and division, ruling out racial segregation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxism-Leninism sees the state as class power, but the Party now describes its state as one 'of the people, by the people and for the people' (Art. 2), so adherents split.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Art. 63 encourages new and recycled energy, while Vietnam also relies on coal and oil for growth; the sources give no clear stance.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The sources do not discuss immigrants; Art. 5 protects each nationality's culture within the nation.

elite-replacement.rationale: Nothing in the programme supports this conspiracy claim, and Art. 5 stresses equality of nationalities; inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: Art. 7 sets universal equal direct secret suffrage for the Assembly but party-list proportionality is moot under single-party leadership; sources give no stance.

national-mission.rationale: The Party presents Vietnam's path as its own, built on independence, and does not claim a mission to spread its system abroad.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Art. 26 asserts gender equality, but sources neither endorse nor deny a structural patriarchy.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Trong names 'corruption, bureaucracy and degradation' as the main risk to the ruling party, so adherents see corruption as a risk to combat, not a settled condition of the elite.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Art. 58 refers to family planning but nothing endorses eugenic limits; inferred from the rights language.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Art. 65 requires the armed forces to protect the Party and regime; legal accountability for past killings is not a stated aim.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Art. 51-52 make the State the coordinator of the economy with a leading state sector and Art. 58-61 give it duties in health, education and housing.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Art. 5 and 16 forbid discrimination between nationalities and the programme treats them as equal and united.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Art. 16 says all citizens are equal before the law and none shall be discriminated against in political, civic, economic, cultural or social life.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The Party builds socialism through a national path of Vietnamese socialism and does not make its success depend on revolution elsewhere.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The sources do not address the settler-colonial framing.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Art. 16 equal before the law and Art. 24 equal treatment of religions imply one civil law; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Art. 24 protects freedom to follow any religion or none, though the law restricts exploitation of religion; inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Nothing in the programme or culture supports it and Art. 24 forbids religious exemptions from state law.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Education under Art. 61 is a state policy within a secular, Marxist-Leninist framework, with no provision for religious instruction.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Classical doctrine asked this, but current texts stress peace, integration and a socialist rule-of-law state rather than a strengthening-for-encirclement argument.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Art. 2 says all state powers belong to the people and Art. 4 says the Party submits to people's supervision, though consent is expressed through Party-led channels.

trade-surplus.rationale: Doi Moi turned toward export growth, but the sources do not state a doctrine of surplus-seeking.

population-transfer.rationale: Art. 5 forbids national discrimination and division and promotes the equality of nationalities.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The state rests on revolutionary force and armed forces (Art. 64-65) and Art. 32 allows compulsory requisition, so an absolute rule against initiating force is not held.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Trong stresses solidarity and consensus and says the model is not capitalist, even though Art. 51 has sectors 'cooperate and compete', so struggle between peoples is rejected.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Art. 4 makes the Communist Party the leading force and only one party exists, so parties challenging the constitutional order are barred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Sources do not take up republican freedom theory; Art. 3 aims for a 'free and happy life'.

separated-powers.rationale: Art. 2 says power is 'unified' and distributed to bodies that coordinate, and Art. 8 sets democratic centralism, explicitly not the Western separation of powers.

vanguard-party.rationale: Art. 4 declares the Party 'the vanguard of the Vietnamese working class' and the leading force of the State, grounded in Marxism-Leninism.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Art. 58 and 59 give priority policies in health and social welfare to the poor, minorities and disadvantaged.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Art. 59 has the State develop housing; Doi Moi privatised much state housing, but no source states a right-to-buy policy.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes are legally regulated and need to follow procedure through Party-linked unions (Art. 9, 57); inferred, as sources do not discuss strike law.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Art. 58 has family planning policy, but the Party blames institutions and development levels more than population; inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Trong's call for 'a culture of unity in diversity' and Art. 5 on equal solidary nationalities reject this view.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Art. 7 provides for elections and the Party selects cadres, so lottery is alien to the system.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Art. 14 allows human rights restrictions in imperative circumstances of national defence, security and order, accepting emergency limits.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Art. 52 has the State coordinate the economy, and the state can manage prices; inferred as a tool in scarcity, not explicitly discussed.

party-controls-media.rationale: Art. 60 describes mass media as serving the construction and defence of the Fatherland under the Party's leading role, so government control is accepted.

party-commands-army.rationale: Art. 65 requires the armed forces to show absolute loyalty to the Party as well as the State and to protect the Party and socialist regime.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The sources do not discuss naturalisation periods.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Elected representatives are not paid as average workers in Vietnam and the programme does not demand this; inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Art. 8 states the principle of democratic centralism, under which adopted decisions bind all members once decided.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Trong stresses independence and self-reliance and national sovereignty, so pooling sovereignty in a supranational union is rejected.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Art. 88 gives the President duties over the armed forces and government appointments, but the Party leads the army (Art. 65) and the Assembly elects the President, so the statement only partly fits.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; Art. 24 treats all religions as equal before the law.

clerical-rule.rationale: Art. 4 gives leadership to the Communist Party and Art. 24 separates belief from state power.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Classical Leninism asked this but current policy is national defence of the Fatherland (Art. 44, 45), so working people supporting their own state is the norm.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Art. 60 calls for 'healthy spiritual demands' in literature and art and Art. 14 allows restrictions for social morality; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The Party has debated term limits for leaders and the Constitution sets Assembly terms; sources do not settle the point.

recall-officials.rationale: Art. 7 says Assembly and People's Council deputies shall be removed from office when no longer worthy of the people's confidence.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Vietnam keeps no formal alliances (the 'no alliances' policy), so ending them is moot; no stated position.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Art. 59 has the State develop housing for all and Art. 32 protects property and enterprise; banning rental is nowhere proposed.

people-in-arms.rationale: Art. 66 calls for a regular army with strong self-defence militia, a mix that rejects replacing the professional army with the armed citizenry.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The programme builds industrialisation and modernisation, not rural moral primacy.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Vietnam was reunified under the Party in 1975-76; the statement concerns the unity of the nation, which the Constitution preamble celebrates.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Trong calls for knowledge-based development and Art. 61 prioritises education, so anti-intellectualism is not an adherent stance.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Trong's 'culture of unity in diversity, on the basis of progressive and humanistic values' and Art. 5 equality of nationalities support equal standing of cultures.

death-penalty.rationale: Vietnam retains the death penalty for grave crimes including terrorism, within a legal framework the State defends; inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Art. 26 promotes gender equality and Art. 61 makes education a state priority; inferred as consistent with state schooling.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The Party follows scientific socialism and Art. 62 prioritises science, so creationism has no place in schools.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Art. 14 and 60 allow restriction for social morality and promote 'healthy' culture, and pornography is illegal in Vietnam.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Art. 17 defines citizens as persons with Vietnamese nationality and Vietnamese citizenship law is based on descent; inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Art. 5 gives every nationality the right to use its own language and writing, and the State develops conditions for minorities.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Art. 24 forbids using religion to violate the laws, so general laws apply without religious exemption.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Art. 60 promotes a 'healthy' culture and Art. 14 allows restriction for social morality, which favours conformity to socialist cultural norms.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Vietnam itself borrows and repays and the sources do not take a stance on cancelling others' debts.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Trong ties national independence to socialism as the 'fundamental guideline' of the revolution, linking political independence to socialist change.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The Constitution is revised by the National Assembly under Party leadership (Art. 120), not a separate constituent assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Doi Moi paired economic liberalisation with refusal of political reform, accepting restraint of political freedoms to preserve stability for development.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: As a developing nation the Party advocates international cooperation and development; inferred, as the sources do not set a duty to give aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Vietnam has no nuclear weapons and its foreign policy stresses peace and independence; inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Art. 87 has the National Assembly elect the State President from among its members, not the people directly.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Art. 55 has the State uniformly manage finance and guarantee the national currency, with no independence from the government.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Art. 5 stresses territorial integrity but the sources do not address land-for-peace deals.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Art. 32 permits requisition for national interest and Art. 54 lets land be recovered for public interest, and Art. 15 limits rights by national interests.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Trong calls the Soviet collapse a failure to follow the proper path but not state capitalism; the Party views the USSR as an attempt at socialism that went wrong.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Art. 63 commits the State to act on environmental protection and climate response but no source states a precautionary standard.

collective-defense.rationale: Vietnam keeps a 'no military alliances' stance, so it has no collective defence doctrine; no stated view.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Vietnam stresses sovereignty and territorial integrity but sources take no stand on annexed territories generally.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Art. 24 forbids using religion against the law and religious bodies operate under State management in Vietnam.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The President is elected by the Assembly and is typically a Party leader, so the nonpartisan symbolic model is not used; no stated view.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Art. 5 forbids acts of national division and Art. 64-65 give the armed forces the duty to protect unity and territorial integrity.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The Party has accepted this for other states' regions (Hong Kong) but it is not Vietnamese doctrine; no stated position.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The state is a republic of the people (Art. 2) and the Party is Marxist, so divine descent is rejected.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Trong says growth must come with 'equality in every stage', implying progressive taxation.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marxism-Leninism holds that circumstances shape consciousness, a view Trong's scientific socialism assumes; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Art. 8 says the State governs society by the Constitution and laws and Art. 4(3) says Party members act within the framework of the Constitution and laws.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Art. 2 and 4 assign rule to the Party-led people, not a mixture of few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: Collective leadership is stressed and the Party has criticised personality cults, though Ho Chi Minh is venerated; inferred.

equal-parenting.rationale: Sources do not discuss child custody.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Trong says socialism seeks consensus over antagonism, and that struggle is 'between the old and the new', not a continuing class war with Party leaders restoring capitalism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Doi Moi stopped collectivization and granted household use rights; further redistribution of estates is not on the programme, and Art. 53 already puts land under state ownership.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Foreign policy stresses sovereignty and Art. 5 defines the nation by its territory, so claims on territory abroad are rejected.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Art. 24 lets everyone follow any religion or none.

women-must-cover.rationale: Art. 26 guarantees women's equal rights and the programme does not impose dress codes.

common-currency.rationale: Art. 55 makes the dong the national currency and the State guarantees its value; a shared currency is not sought.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Policy centres on the sovereign Vietnamese nation and independence, so cross-border unions of kin peoples are not sought.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Art. 5 gives nationalities cultural rights but no self-governing institutions beyond those of the unified state.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The Party states its model follows historical materialism, that socialism emerges only when material conditions are developed enough.

ban-cartels.rationale: Art. 51 says sectors compete in accordance with the law and Art. 52 has the State regulate the market; inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: The state economy leads and the State coordinates the economy (Art. 51-52), so public support for failing state banks and firms is accepted.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Courts in Vietnam answer to the Assembly and Party, not independent from the majority; no stated view on liberal democratic courts.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Art. 26 has the State guarantee equal gender opportunities and promote women's role; inferred support for near-parity quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Trong calls the market economy 'well integrated with the world' and Doi Moi opened to trade and investment, rejecting autarky.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Art. 50, 57 and 63 stress protecting labour and the environment, so standards in trade are consistent; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Doi Moi restored material incentives in agriculture and industry as the main spur, abandoning the moral-incentive economy of the earlier period.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Current doctrine follows historical materialism, which holds that conditions must develop, not foco-style armed groups.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Art. 16 forbids discrimination in social life and Art. 2 vests power in the people, so hereditary privilege is rejected.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Art. 60 calls for culture imbued with national identity, and patriotic loyalty is a duty (Art. 44); inferred.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Art. 58, 61 give priority policies to national minorities, which the state treats as legitimate equality measures.

public-money-creation.rationale: Art. 55 puts the State in charge of currency and public finance, in line with public money creation; inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Marxist doctrine expects crises but the Party accepts working with capitalist economies and treats capitalism as able to develop productive forces.

delink-world-market.rationale: Trong calls for a market economy 'well integrated with the world', so delinking is rejected.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Art. 16 bans discrimination in political, civic, economic, cultural and social life.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Art. 14 and 15 allow rights to be restricted for national interests and the Assembly can amend the Constitution, so an entrenched limiting bill is not the model.

elective-rulers.rationale: Art. 7 provides for elected representatives and Art. 87 has the Assembly elect the President, so rulers are chosen by selection, not inheritance.

minority-veto.rationale: Art. 8 sets democratic centralism, under which decisions bind the minority once adopted.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Art. 46 stresses duty to obey the Constitution and law, and resistance outside the Party-led channels is not endorsed.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Art. 69 describes the National Assembly as the highest organ of state power, though the Party leads it.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Art. 63 protects biodiversity and nature, a minimal concern; inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not directly addressed; consistent with regulated use under Art. 63 protection of nature.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Art. 15 stresses duties of citizens and Art. 59 social welfare duties of State, but the wealthy are not framed as charity patrons.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Art. 6 and 15 stress citizens' participation and duty to the community, so withdrawal is not endorsed.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Art. 60 treats media as serving national construction, but the sources do not hold that mass culture pacifies people; no stated view.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not addressed; the Party claims to rule with the people's trust through consent and organisation.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Marxist theory suggests it, but present policy seeks integration and investment, and Trong stresses cooperation; no stated claim.

native-born-offices.rationale: Art. 17 defines citizens by nationality and offices are for citizens (not specified as native-born); inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: Trong calls socialism in Vietnam a path shaped by national conditions and independence 'the fundamental guideline', a statement that each party finds its own road.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Trong calls for 'independence, self-reliance' but combined with integration and attracting foreign investment (s4), so aid and investment are used.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Art. 5 declares all nationalities equal and rejects descent-based political leadership.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Constitution preamble mentions anti-imperialist struggle but there is no founding anti-fascist clause.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The Party rejects equating fascism with communism, as it draws its own legitimacy from the communist revolution.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; Marxist history treats slavery as central to that war; inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Official sources do not discuss contested monuments; Vietnam keeps its revolutionary monuments but has no stated doctrine on condemned figures.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Art. 26 guarantees equal rights; the sources do not take up this issue.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Vietnamese policy focuses on protecting women; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Trong presents Vietnamese socialism as suited to Vietnam's conditions and criticises the multiparty Western model.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Art. 65 puts the army under the Party's leadership, not an autonomous guardian role.

paid-care-work.rationale: Art. 26 and 58 stress women's roles and State care but nothing explicit; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Art. 37(3) has the State, family and society respect and take care of old people, and cultural tradition stresses care for parents.

office-by-exam.rationale: Cadre selection includes examination for civil service posts, in a system of Party appointment; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Art. 51 gives the state sector the leading role in strategic industries, consistent with protecting them from foreign takeover.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Vietnamese law provides for divorce by mutual consent; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Art. 7 lets deputies be removed when they lose confidence, but democratic centralism binds officials to higher bodies; mixed.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Art. 34 and 59 provide social insurance and a social security system run by the State.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Art. 55 says budget items must be estimated and provided by law, which the National Assembly approves.

single-official-language.rationale: Art. 5 makes Vietnamese the national language but every nationality has the right to use its own language.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Art. 53-54 make land owned by the entire people, with individuals holding land-use rights from the State.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Art. 53 makes land state property, so foreigners cannot own land, only lease use rights.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Art. 16 bans discrimination but no source supports an outcome-based test.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Art. 56 requires saving and anti-luxury behaviour from officials and individuals.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Foreign policy rests on independence and non-interference, which rejects arming insurgents abroad.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Respect for independence and sovereignty rules out sending troops into an allied state against its will.

corporate-influence.rationale: Trong criticises the 'dictatorship of capitalist cartels' behind Western multiparty systems, implying corporate sway over politics.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Art. 14 allows rights restrictions for national security, and the state controls NGO funding in practice; inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Art. 58 covers population policy, and Vietnam recently moved to encourage more births; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Art. 54 gives the State land management; local residents-only limits are not discussed.

job-guarantee.rationale: Art. 35 declares a right to work but the State only provides 'favorable conditions' (Art. 57), not an employer-of-last-resort guarantee.

democratic-peace.rationale: The sources do not take up democratic peace theory, and the Party criticises Western multiparty democracy, so there is no stated position.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Art. 46 makes it the citizen's duty to obey the Constitution and the law.

non-intervention.rationale: Trong lists 'independence, self-reliance, peace, cooperation and development' as the foreign policy guideline.

industrial-unions.rationale: Art. 9 names the Vietnam Trade Union as a single national body; craft versus industry is not discussed.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Art. 5 forbids discrimination against nationalities and promotes solidarity.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Art. 36 says the State protects marriage and family and sets legal principles for marriage, so abolishing it is opposed.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Art. 25 grants citizens the right to access to information, in accordance with the law.

local-production.rationale: The market economy is 'well integrated with the world', so mainly local production is not the aim.

informal-organisation.rationale: The Party and Fatherland Front organise politics through permanent bodies (Art. 4, 9), opposing informal organisation.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not addressed; Vietnam joins treaties and also stresses sovereignty.

religious-nation.rationale: Art. 5 defines the nation by all nationalities and Art. 24 equalises religions.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Independence and equality among states are core foreign policy principles, rejecting tribute-style deference.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Art. 52 and 55 stress unity of the national economy and redistribution via the central budget, which plays the leading role.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Art. 32 protects ownership of lawful income, savings, housing and chattels.

defeat-communism.rationale: The state is led by a communist party that holds communism as a long-term goal.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Doi Moi created a hybrid health system, but the model keeps public leadership in services, so adherents are partly split.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marxist-Leninist doctrine holds religion fades as conditions improve, though policy respects belief (Art. 24); inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Party explains the market stage as developing productive forces that capitalism supplies, a necessary stage for socialism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Art. 26 guarantees equality in law; the sources do not link it to economic transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: Art. 58 shares care between State, society, family and citizen, so not wholly public.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Art. 5 protects Vietnamese and minority languages but purging loanwords is not stated policy.

treaties-binding.rationale: The sources say nothing on treaties between a government and nations within its borders; Art. 5 gives minorities cultural rights, not treaty status.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Doi Moi ended obligatory cooperatives and the model centres on national market institutions, not small self-governing communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Art. 5 stresses minority development; inferred, though the state has run internal resettlement programmes.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Party names communism as the ultimate goal and its model as a transition to socialism, not a third course.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Vietnam asserts historic sovereignty over some territory (South China Sea) but the sources do not discuss the principle.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Nothing in the programme supports it; inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Vietnam does not criminalise same-sex relations; inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Art. 4 sets one party's leading role and the state restricts independent opposition organisations; supported by the system.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Art. 24 protects religious freedom for all religions equally.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The state's origins are in the anticolonial revolution, and Art. 5 equalises nationalities.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Art. 4 and 24 reject religious sources of legitimacy.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Trong calls democracy 'the nature of the socialist regime' and says the people are owners, and Art. 6 includes direct democracy.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The Party's analysis is class-based and does not adopt intersectional framing; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Vietnam has only recently debated recognising transgender people; inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; Vietnamese law does not allow it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The Party insists on its Marxist-Leninist identity and socialist orientation, so it does not treat left and right as outdated.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist foundations include alienation, but the sources do not state it; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Art. 24 makes all religions equal before the law.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Art. 2 says state powers belong to the people.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The Constitution and Party texts do not discuss religious dress in state institutions, so the Party has no stated position.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The sources do not discuss nondisclosure agreements or arbitration; Art. 26 bans sex discrimination but gives no view on procedure.

social-market-economy.rationale: The model is socialist-oriented with a leading state sector, not a German-style social market; Art. 51-52 call for market rules with social aims, so it partly agrees.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Art. 64-66 build a revolutionary people's army.

rich-first.rationale: Doi Moi allowed some to get rich first, the Deng-style 'let some get rich' approach used to reach growth, with regional and urban gaps accepted.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Vietnam's 'independence, self-reliance, peace' foreign policy matches its non-aligned posture.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The state is a republic where office is by Party and Assembly selection, so hereditary succession is opposed.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Art. 55 puts credit in the State's hands and the market economy uses banks, so mutual interest-free credit is not part of the model.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Vietnam rejected World Bank structural adjustment that required privatising state enterprises, but accepted other advice, so the position is mixed.

property-franchise.rationale: Art. 27 gives every citizen aged eighteen the vote.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The ecofeminist link between domination of women and of nature is not addressed in any Party text I opened.

reification.rationale: Marxist idea but not stated in the sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Trong criticises 'dictatorship of capitalist cartels' behind Western multiparty politics, in line with the claim.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Art. 8 requires the State to govern by the Constitution and laws as a 'socialist rule of law State'.

racial-franchise.rationale: Art. 27 and 16 give all citizens equal voting rights.

online-participation.rationale: The sources do not address online deliberation; Art. 6 allows direct democracy in general, but no internet-voting position is stated.

open-government-data.rationale: Art. 25 gives access to information in accordance with law, but open decision records are not addressed.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Art. 24 treats all religions as equal before the law and bars discrimination.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Art. 5 forbids national discrimination and Art. 24 equality of religions.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The state was founded in an anticolonial revolution and its foreign policy rests on independence and equality among states, so rule over 'less advanced' societies is rejected.

patriotic-education.rationale: Art. 44 requires loyalty to the Fatherland, Art. 60 calls for people who are 'profoundly patriotic', and Art. 37(2) has the State educate youth in national tradition and civic consciousness.

missingStatements.text: A country can build socialism by first developing a market economy with private enterprise under Communist Party leadership.
missingStatements.rationale: This is the defining claim of the doctrine: the market economy is a transitional stage that builds the productive forces socialism needs, directed by the Party.

missingStatements.text: Private enterprises and investments should be guaranteed by law against nationalisation.
missingStatements.rationale: Article 51 states that private possessions and investments are protected and not subject to nationalisation, and Doi Moi's investment law ruled out nationalisation of foreign assets.
missingStatements.declined: Overlaps property-fundamental, which the audit answers -1, so a merge would conflict; a protection-from-nationalisation clause is a narrow legal detail.

notes: Scholars disagree whether the model is market socialism or East Asian state capitalism; the Party calls it a transitional economy, not socialism. Answers follow official Party and constitutional texts; actual practice, such as corruption or inequality, may diverge.
